subject.title: fix(agents): stop stable tool argument churn

question: Should the generic global loop breaker be allowed to treat multiple distinct argument variants with independently stable results as no progress, or must it require a stronger cross-variant semantic invariant?
rationale: The current PR makes a safety-policy tradeoff for every user who enables loop detection, but the repository evidence supplied here does not define when distinct successful operations should be considered equivalent enough to veto.

options.title: Require stronger no-progress evidence
options.body: Revise the detector so stable outcomes across distinct argument variants alone cannot trip the global veto; this preserves legitimate repeated operations by default.

options.title: Accept the broad safety heuristic
options.body: Keep the current per-variant rule and explicitly accept that some enabled users' recurring same-tool workflows may be stopped after the global threshold.

recommendation.title: Require stronger no-progress evidence
recommendation.body: Revise the detector so stable outcomes across distinct argument variants alone cannot trip the global veto; this preserves legitimate repeated operations by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed detector design in the available branch history, although a current-main agents-runtime owner should confirm the policy direction.
